Text.name: guidelines
Text.value: Read the question and answer, then determine if the answer demonstrates SCAFFOLDING.

Text.name: scaff_step1_header
Text.value: 📖 STEP 1: DEFINITION - What is scaffolding?

Text.name: scaff_step1_def
Text.value: Scaffolding means the explanation BUILDS UNDERSTANDING by introducing ideas in order of increasing complexity.

Text.name: scaff_complexity_header
Text.value: WHAT MAKES AN IDEA 'SIMPLER' vs 'MORE COMPLEX'?

Text.name: scaff_complex1_header
Text.value: 1. STANDALONE vs DEPENDENT:

Text.name: scaff_complex1_simple
Text.value: - Simple: 'Atoms are tiny particles' (understood alone)

Text.name: scaff_complex1_complex
Text.value: - Complex: 'Electrons orbit the nucleus' (requires knowing what atoms are)

Text.name: scaff_complex2_header
Text.value: 2. FEWER vs MORE PREREQUISITES:

Text.name: scaff_complex2_simple
Text.value: - Simple: 'Plants need sunlight' (common knowledge)

Text.name: scaff_complex2_complex
Text.value: - Complex: 'Chlorophyll absorbs photons to split water molecules' (requires chemistry)

Text.name: scaff_complex3_header
Text.value: 3. CONCRETE vs ABSTRACT:

Text.name: scaff_complex3_simple
Text.value: - Simple: 'Ice melts when heated' (observable)

Text.name: scaff_complex3_complex
Text.value: - Complex: 'Phase transitions occur when thermal energy exceeds intermolecular bonds'

Text.name: scaff_complex4_header
Text.value: 4. SINGLE vs COMBINED CONCEPTS:

Text.name: scaff_complex4_simple
Text.value: - Simple: 'DNA stores genetic information' (one idea)

Text.name: scaff_complex4_complex
Text.value: - Complex: 'DNA replication errors during cell division cause mutations that may lead to cancer' (4 concepts)

Text.name: scaff_min_req
Text.value: ⚠️ MINIMUM REQUIREMENT: At least 2 ideas where the second DEPENDS ON or DEEPENS the first.

Text.name: scaff_single_fact
Text.value: A SINGLE fact or definition is NOT scaffolding (nothing to build on).

Text.name: scaff_step2_header
Text.value: ✅ STEP 2: Examples of SCAFFOLDING PRESENT (Mark Yes):

Text.name: scaff_present_short_header
Text.value: SHORT ANSWER examples:

Text.name: scaff_present_ex1
Text.value: - 'Cells are the basic building blocks of life. DNA inside cells contains instructions for making proteins.'

Text.name: scaff_present_ex1_why
Text.value: → First establishes cells, then zooms into DNA - builds from whole to part

Text.name: scaff_present_ex2
Text.value: - 'When you heat water, molecules move faster. This is why boiling water evaporates.'

Text.name: scaff_present_ex2_why
Text.value: → First explains mechanism (molecules), then applies to observable phenomenon

Text.name: scaff_present_ex3
Text.value: - 'Gravity pulls things toward Earth. That's why we don't float away.'

Text.name: scaff_present_ex3_why
Text.value: → First states rule, then connects to everyday experience

Text.name: scaff_present_long_header
Text.value: LONGER ANSWER example:

Text.name: scaff_present_long
Text.value: - 'Two facts motivate my research—first, diverse systems are healthier... My research asks if it matters that species are being gained and lost... By manipulating plant number and type, I can begin to uncover the mechanisms...'

Text.name: scaff_present_long_why
Text.value: → Starts with motivation → poses question → describes method (clear progression)

Text.name: scaff_step3_header
Text.value: ❌ STEP 3: Examples of SCAFFOLDING ABSENT (Mark No):

Text.name: scaff_absent_single_header
Text.value: SINGLE FACT (nothing to build on):

Text.name: scaff_absent_single1
Text.value: - 'Photosynthesis converts sunlight into energy.' → Just one idea, no building possible

Text.name: scaff_absent_single2
Text.value: - 'The mitochondria is the powerhouse of the cell.' → Single definition, no progression

Text.name: scaff_absent_list_header
Text.value: UNORDERED LIST of facts:

Text.name: scaff_absent_list
Text.value: - 'DNA contains genes. Proteins are made from amino acids. Cells divide through mitosis.'

Text.name: scaff_absent_list_why
Text.value: → Multiple facts but no logical order or building between them

Text.name: scaff_absent_allonce_header
Text.value: ALL AT ONCE (no progression):

Text.name: scaff_absent_allonce
Text.value: - 'Quantum entanglement occurs when particles become correlated such that measuring one instantaneously affects the other...'

Text.name: scaff_absent_allonce_why
Text.value: → All concepts crammed together with no build-up

Text.name: scaff_absent_reverse_header
Text.value: COMPLEX BEFORE SIMPLE:

Text.name: scaff_absent_reverse
Text.value: - 'The non-local correlations from entanglement happen because... basically, particles can be connected.'

Text.name: scaff_absent_reverse_why
Text.value: → Starts with the hard part, then gives the simple explanation

Text.name: scaff_absent_flow_header
Text.value: ⚠️ LOGICAL FLOW WITHOUT BUILDING (NOT scaffolding):

Text.name: scaff_absent_flow1
Text.value: - 'Scientists collected samples. They analyzed the samples. They published their findings.'

Text.name: scaff_absent_flow1_why
Text.value: → Ideas flow logically but stay at same complexity level - no building

Text.name: scaff_absent_flow2
Text.value: - 'The experiment tested temperature. Results showed higher temps increased reaction speed.'

Text.name: scaff_absent_flow2_why
Text.value: → Coherent narrative, but each sentence is equally complex - no scaffolding

Text.name: scaff_absent_flow3
Text.value: - 'Photosynthesis happens in leaves. It uses sunlight. Plants need it to survive.'

Text.name: scaff_absent_flow3_why
Text.value: → Related facts that flow, but none requires understanding the previous one

Text.name: scaff_key_distinction
Text.value: KEY DISTINCTION: Scaffolding requires INCREASING DEPTH, not just logical coherence.

Text.name: scaff_step4_header
Text.value: ⚠️ STEP 4: Common edge cases

Text.name: scaff_edge_short_header
Text.value: SHORT ≠ NO SCAFFOLDING:

Text.name: scaff_edge_short1
Text.value: - A 2-sentence answer CAN have scaffolding if idea #1 prepares for idea #2

Text.name: scaff_edge_short2
Text.value: - Length doesn't matter; logical ordering does

Text.name: scaff_edge_trans_header
Text.value: TRANSITION WORDS DON'T GUARANTEE SCAFFOLDING:

Text.name: scaff_edge_trans_note
Text.value: - 'because', 'therefore', 'this means' can indicate building, but not always

Text.name: scaff_edge_trans_yes_header
Text.value: WITH transitions, IS scaffolding:

Text.name: scaff_edge_trans_yes
Text.value: - 'Gravity pulls objects toward Earth. Because of this, dropped objects fall.' → Simple rule first, then applies it

Text.name: scaff_edge_trans_no_header
Text.value: WITH transitions, NOT scaffolding:

Text.name: scaff_edge_trans_no1
Text.value: - 'Entropy increases because systems tend toward disorder because energy spreads out.' → All same complexity

Text.name: scaff_edge_trans_no2
Text.value: - 'Quantum tunneling occurs because wavefunctions extend beyond barriers.' → Single complex statement

Text.name: scaff_edge_trans_without_header
Text.value: WITHOUT transitions, IS scaffolding:

Text.name: scaff_edge_trans_without
Text.value: - 'Atoms have electrons. Electrons carry charge. Charge creates electricity.' → Clear simple→complex progression

Text.name: scaff_edge_chrono_header
Text.value: CHRONOLOGICAL ORDER ≠ SCAFFOLDING:

Text.name: scaff_edge_chrono1
Text.value: - 'First I added water, then I heated it, then it boiled' is just a sequence

Text.name: scaff_edge_chrono2
Text.value: - Scaffolding requires conceptual building, not just time order

Text.name: scaff_edge_flow_header
Text.value: LOGICAL FLOW ≠ SCAFFOLDING:

Text.name: scaff_edge_flow1
Text.value: - A well-organized answer can flow smoothly without scaffolding

Text.name: scaff_edge_flow2
Text.value: - Scaffolding requires each idea to be MORE COMPLEX than the previous

Text.name: scaff_edge_flow3
Text.value: - If all ideas are at the same complexity level, it's NOT scaffolding (even if coherent)

Text.name: scaff_final_header
Text.value: ⚖️ FINAL DECISION:

Text.name: scaff_final_yes
Text.value: ✅ Mark Yes: Ideas are ordered from simple→complex, with building/dependence

Text.name: scaff_final_no
Text.value: ❌ Mark No: Single idea, random order, complex-before-simple, or same-complexity flow

TextArea.name: scaffolding_reasoning
TextArea.placeholder: Please explain your decision. Describe what progression you found (or didn't find) - does the answer build from simpler to more complex ideas? Reference the guidelines above.
